projects.flagshipProject: Book of Record + Financial Activity Model + Financial Calculation Platform
projects.description: Wealthsimple's Book of Record is the authoritative record of client money and assets across the Trade, Cash, Managed Investing and Tax products: every movement becomes a balanced accounting entry, and everything a client sees about their money is derived from it. The client base runs to millions of accounts and the ledger carries every movement across all of them. A client moves money or places a trade in the app; the intent enters through the Financial Activity Model, the single validated and idempotent write funnel; it is committed to the ledger as balanced debit and credit entries; the Financial Calculation Platform and its materialized read models recompute the derived figures; and the app surfaces are read from those. Behind that sits an event-driven estate with a workflow engine driving long-running money movement, and a legacy monolith still being decomposed behind anti-corruption layers. It touches the front end (app balances, activity feeds and internal operations tooling), the back end (the write funnel, posting pipelines and workflow orchestration), the data/AI side (streaming calculation, feature extraction from ledger events, anomaly detection), the infrastructure layer (deployment, inference serving and observability), and the security and governance layer (redaction, access controls and regulated financial controls).
projects.notes: Publicly documented by Wealthsimple: Book of Record / Financial Activity Model / ledger / Financial Calculation Platform (engineering.wealthsimple.com/inside-the-book-of-record); Machine Learning Platform with sub-15-minute model deployment; NVIDIA-backed AI Inference Platform, 30+ models and 247M predictions in 12 months; LLM Gateway, 72,000+ requests at launch and ~500 daily users; Flow-to-TypeScript migration of 700,000+ lines across 40+ repos; Kafka event backbone, Ruby on Rails monolith decomposition, Java/Kotlin/Node.js/Python services and a JSON-defined workflow engine (engineering.wealthsimple.com, medium.com/wealthsimple). All figures are COMPANY/PLATFORM figures describing the project universe, NOT the candidate's personal attribution. FIGURES REMOVED (2026-08-22): this was the only anchor in the repo carrying hard numbers, so the prompt's preference for figures already in summary_lines reproduced the identical 700,000 / 15 minutes / 30+ / 247 million set in every resume generated for him. Scale is now qualitative and the prompt writes its own figures per run. The underlying public sources are still cited above; do not paste the numbers back into the description. HEDGES REMOVED (2026-08-22): replacing the sourced figures with qualitative scale backfired -- this anchor carried 8 hedged phrases against 0-2 in every other anchor, and the model copied them through verbatim ("dozens of production models", "hundreds of millions of predictions a year", "hundreds of engineers a day") and treated that as having quantified, shipping a direct section with zero real metrics. The scale language is gone entirely; this anchor now names systems the way the other three do and the prompt writes its own figures. RESHAPED TO A STAGE (2026-08-23): removed the stack inventory sentence (microservices on AWS, Apache Kafka, Kotlin/Python/Node.js, JSON-defined workflow engine, Ruby on Rails, Flow-to-TypeScript, NVIDIA/GPU) and the tool names inside the layer sweep. The situations they described are kept as situations -- an event-driven estate, a workflow engine, a legacy monolith behind anti-corruption layers -- so the model can name whichever stack the JD asks for while the flow and every Wealthsimple product name stay intact. Measured reason: anchor bulk and named stacks crowd out JD material in a fixed 10-12 bullet budget, and deepankar's 797-char stack-free anchor pulled 15 of its 16 technologies straight from the reframed_jd. SCALE CONTEXT (2026-08-23): one clause naming the order of magnitude this employer operates at. Not an achievement figure and not claimable as a metric -- the prompt already rules that vague quantifiers do not satisfy the metric requirement. It exists so invented figures anchor to THIS company's size instead of the model's generic default, which is what made three profiles independently pick 190 ms on the same JD.

Suncore, then operating as Sunroc Corporation, was modernizing the software and data workflows supporting its construction and materials businesses across the Intermountain West. The initiative connected customer and sales workflows with estimating, quoting, project and job-cost information, dispatch and fleet telemetry, materials operations, billing, and enterprise reporting so field and office teams could work from one consistent view of operational data instead of systems that had grown up separately. Cloud-based customer and operational platforms brought mobile access to crews and sales staff, while construction ERP capabilities carried project management, cost control, procurement and financial workflows. The hard problems were integrating field systems with corporate platforms, keeping job-cost and billing data reconcilable across sources, and making operational data trustworthy enough for teams to quote and dispatch from. It spans enterprise applications, backend integrations and APIs, operational and financial data pipelines, mobile and web workflows, reporting, reliability and security.
bullets: Built backend services and integrations that connected the cloud CRM used by sales and estimating with dispatch, telematics and job-cost systems, replacing manual re-keying between platforms that had grown up separately.

Delivered quoting and project workflows for ready-mix and construction operations, surfacing customer history and live operational data together so sales teams could price and commit work without leaving the application.
Developed data pipelines consolidating project, job-cost, materials and fleet telemetry into reporting models that gave operations and finance one reconcilable view across business units.
Built mobile-accessible field workflows and the APIs behind them so crews and dispatchers could record and retrieve operational data on site rather than routing everything through the office.
projects.notes: Company was Sunroc Corporation during this period; rebranded to Suncore Construction & Materials in 2025. Anchor is grounded in publicly reported Clyde Companies / Sunroc modernization (cloud CRM tailored to ready-mix, dispatch and telematics integration, mobile access) plus secondary reporting of a construction ERP implementation in 2018. Bullets are INFERRED from that public record, not supplied by the candidate - confirm before any live submission.

projects.description: CIBC expanded its digital banking platform through this period from traditional online banking into a major mobile financial-services channel, launching Canada's first mobile banking application from a major bank in 2010 and then extending it across additional devices, brokerage, mobile web, tablet banking, payments and mobile cheque deposit. Clients could view accounts, transfer funds, pay bills, move money between people, access investing, and increasingly complete banking end to end from a phone. Supporting that required integration between client applications and core banking services, transaction and payment workflows, account and balance data, authentication and authorization, fraud and security controls, and the shared digital-channel services behind every banking experience. The hard problems were availability and correctness on money movement, securing a channel that was new to the bank, and evolving customer-facing applications on top of core systems that could not move at the same pace.
bullets: Built client-facing banking applications and the digital-channel services behind them as CIBC extended from online banking into mobile, covering account access, transfers, bill payment and person-to-person money movement.

Developed integration layers between customer applications and core banking systems, isolating channel development from mainframe release cycles so new digital-channel features could evolve without waiting on core-system release cycles.
Implemented authentication, authorization and transaction security controls for a channel that was new to the bank, working within the audit and regulatory requirements of Canadian retail banking.
Delivered payment and transaction workflows with the availability and correctness guarantees money movement demands, including reconciliation and failure handling on client-initiated transfers.
